ordered_diagnoses: Inflammatory bowel disease-associated interstitial lung disease

facts.raw_span: 3-month history of sacroiliac pain, arthralgias, and lower-limb myalgias
partially responsive to NSAIDs
diagnosed with seronegative spondyloarthropathy (negative HLA-B27)
MRI confirmed bilateral active sacroiliitis
developed a dry cough and dyspnea on moderate exertion
without fever, hemoptysis, chest pain, or other systemic symptoms
afebrile, blood pressure 118/84 mmHg, pulse 96 bpm, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygenation normal on room air
Pulmonary auscultation revealed scant basal “Velcro”-like crackles
Hb 13 g/dL, WBC 4,100/mm³ (neutrophils 2,000, lymphocytes 1,400), eosinophils 50/mm³, platelets 325,000/mm³
AST, ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, and BUN were within normal limits

High-resolution chest CT showed ground-glass interstitial infiltrates with a centrifugal distribution, predominantly in the upper lobes, and a mosaic pattern of disseminated attenuation without lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion
GeneXpert for Mycobacterium tuberculosis and methenamine silver stain were negative
